target.title: fix(mcp): suppress unhandled error on stderr pipe in stdio transport
target.body:
## Summary

MCP stdio transport pipes `child.stderr` to `stderrStream` without an error handler. If the stderr stream emits an error event (EPIPE, I/O failure, resource limit), the unhandled error crashes the Node.js process.

## What Problem This Solves

Stderr pipe errors in MCP child process transport crash the gateway. The `child.stdin` and `child.stdout` streams already have error handlers; `child.stderr` is the only one missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a noop `.on("error", () => {})` handler on `child.stderr` before piping — consistent with the existing error handlers on stdin (line 82) and stdout (line 87).

## User Impact

MCP stdio transport no longer crashes on stderr stream errors.

## Evidence

**Before**: `child.stderr.pipe(stderrStream)` — no error handler — unhandled stream error → process crash

**After**: `child.stderr.on("error", () => {}); child.stderr.pipe(stderrStream)` — error suppressed

**Tests** (7 passed):
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

## Risk

Low. One-line addition. Matches the pattern already used for stdin (line 82) and stdout (line 87) in the same file.
